source_text: Ἡσαΐας λέγων, ὅτι «Ἐκπλυνεῖ Κύριος τὸν ῥύπον τῶν υἱῶν καὶ τῶν θυγατέρων Σιὼν, καὶ τὸ αἷμα ἐκκαθαριεῖ ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν ἐν πνεύματι κρίσεως, καὶ ἐν πνεύματι καύσεως.» Ἆρ' οὖν, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ νοουμένης δικαιοσύνης ὁ τρόπος διαπεραίνοιτο ἂν πρὸς ἡμῶν, ὡς ἔν γε δὴ μόνῳ τῷ διασμήχεσθαι δεῖν; καὶ τὸ ἀρχαίους ἡμᾶς ἀποτρίψασθαι μολυσμούς; ἀρκέσειεν ἂν, εἰπέ μοι, πρὸς δόξαν ἡμῖν ἁγιοπρεπῆ, καὶ ταῖς ἀνωτάτω στεφανώσει τιμαῖς; ἤγουν, ἔσται πως τὰ καθ' ἡμᾶς ἐν ἀμείνοσι, καὶ τοῖς εἰς ἄκρον ἐπαίνοις κατασεμνυνοῦμεν εἰκότως τὰς ἑαυτῶν κεφαλὰς, οἷάπερ τινὰ δωροφορίαν πνευματικὴν, καὶ ἱερὸν ἀληθῶς ἀνάθημα προσκομίζοντες τῷ Θεῷ, τὴν ἐν ἁγιασμῷ καὶ ὁσιότητι ζωὴν, καὶ πνευματικὴν λατρείαν εὖ μάλα διαπεραίνοντες; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οὕτω φημί. {ΚΥΡ.} Καὶ γάρ τοι τὸ χρῆμά ἐστι τοῖς ἱεροῖς συμβαῖνον νόμοις, καὶ Θεῷ κεχαρισμένον, καὶ τῶν ὅτι μάλιστα δεδοκιμασμένων· καταλήγειν μὲν ἔργου παντὸς προστέταχεν ἐν Σαββάτῳ, δρᾷν δὲ δὴ ὅλως ἠφίει τινὰς οὐδ' ὅπως τι οὖν, οὕτω λέγων ἐν τῇ Ἐξόδῳ· «Μνήσθητι τὴν ἡμέραν τῶν Σαββάτων ἁγιάζειν αὐτήν. Ἓξ ἡμέρας ἐργᾶ, καὶ ποιήσεις πάντα τὰ ἔργα σου· τῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ, Σάββατα, ἀνάπαυσις Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ σου, οὐ ποιήσεις ἐν αὐτῇ πᾶν ἔργον.» Τὸν ἐν πνεύματι δηλονότι Σαββατισμὸν τοῦ τύπου κατασημαίνοντος, ὅτε καὶ εἰς κατάληξιν καὶ ἀνακωχὴν παντὸς ἔργου σαρκικοῦ, καὶ μοχθηρῶν σπουδασμάτων, δι' αὐτοῦ κεκλήμεθα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἄχθος ἀποσεισάμενοι, καὶ τὴν ἐκ τῆς φαυλότητος ἀγαπῶντες ἀπόστασιν, καὶ τῶν ἔξω νόμου τὴν ἀργίαν· ἀπελείπετο μὲν γὰρ ὁ τοιόσδε Σαββατισμὸς τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσραήλ. Εἰσβεβήκασι γὰρ οὐδαμῶς εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου φωνήν. Ἡμᾶς δὲ κατέπαυσεν ὁ Χριστὸς, καὶ Σαββατίζειν ἀνέπεισε νοητῶς, ἀνιεμένους εἰς ἀρετὴν, καὶ καλὴν πλημμελημάτων ἀργίαν ἐπιτηδεύοντας. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄριστα ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀλλ' ἐθεσμοθέτει μὲν καὶ πάλαι Θεὸς, τὸ δεῖν ἅπαντας ἀργεῖν ἐν Σαββάτῳ. Πλὴν οἱ τῇ θείᾳ λειτουργίᾳ κατεστεμμένοι, καὶ τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ προσεδρεύειν ἐπιτεταγμένοι, πάλιν ἐτέλουν τὰ ἱερά· καὶ βεβηλοῦντες τὸ Σάββατον, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ Σωτῆρος φωνὴν, ἦσαν ἀναίτιοι, τὴν ἐπὶ τῷ λελύσθαι τὸν νόμον οὐχ ὑπομένοντες γραφήν. Οὐκοῦν ἐπιγείων μὲν σπουδασμάτων καὶ ἡμεῖς αὐτοὶ καταλήξομεν ἐν Χριστῷ, τὸν νοητὸν πληροῦντες Σαββατισμὸν, ἀφεξόμεθα δὲ οὐχὶ τῶν ἱερῶν ἔργων, τοῦ χρῆναι, φημὶ, προσκομίζειν Θεῷ θυσίας πνευματικὰς καὶ νοητὰς δωροφορίας. Ἑπόμενοι δὲ ὥσπερ τοῖς ἴχνεσι τοῦ Χριστοῦ, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, ἑαυτοὺς ἱερεύσομεν, οὐ μηλοσφαγίαις καὶ μόσχων αἵμασι τὸν τῶν ὅλων τιμῶντες Θεὸν, ἑαυτοὺς δὲ μᾶλλον εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀνατιθέντες αὐτῷ. Ἀρέσομεν γὰρ ὑπὲρ μόσχον νέον, κέρατα ἐκφέροντα καὶ ὁπλὰς, κατά γε τὴν τοῦ Ψάλλοντος φωνήν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς διανοῇ· πλὴν ἴθι δὴ πάλιν, καὶ ἐξ
pass_a_gloss: [Isaiah] saying: the Lord will wash out (ἐκπλύνω) the filth (ῥύπος) of the sons and daughters of Zion, and cleanse out (ἐκκαθαρίζω) the blood from their midst in a spirit of judgment (κρίσις) and a spirit of burning (καῦσις) [Isaiah 4:4 LXX]. Then (ἆρ' οὖν), O Palladius, would the manner (τρόπος) of the righteousness (δικαιοσύνη) understood (νοουμένη) in Christ be carried through (διαπεραίνω, opt. + ἄν) by us as in only (μόνῳ) the need to be scoured (διασμήχεσθαι) and to rub off (ἀποτρίβω) ancient defilements (μολυσμοί)? Would it suffice (ἀρκέω, opt.), tell me, for a glory befitting holiness (ἁγιοπρεπής), and crown (στεφανόω, fut.) [us] with the highest honors? Or rather (ἤγουν), will our affairs (τὰ καθ' ἡμᾶς) be in better things (ἐν ἀμείνοσι), and shall we fittingly (εἰκότως) dignify (κατασεμνύνω, fut.) our own heads with praises to the utmost, bringing (προσκομίζω) to God as a spiritual gift-offering (δωροφορία πνευματική) and truly sacred dedication (ἀνάθημα) the life in sanctification (ἁγιασμός) and holiness (ὁσιότης), and carrying out well a spiritual service (λατρεία)? PALL.: So I say (οὕτω φημί). CYR.: For the matter (χρῆμα) agrees (συμβαίνω) with the sacred laws, is pleasing (χαρίζομαι, perf. ptc.) to God, and among the most approved (δεδοκιμασμένα). [He/the law] ordered (προστάσσω) ceasing (καταλήγειν) from every work on the Sabbath, and let (ἀφίημι, impf.) no one do (δρᾶν) anything whatever, saying in Exodus [20:8–10 LXX]: remember the day of the Sabbaths to sanctify it; six days you shall work and do all your works; the seventh day, Sabbaths, rest (ἀνάπαυσις) to the Lord your God; you shall not do in it any work. The type (τύπος) plainly signifying (κατασημαίνω) the Sabbath-keeping (σαββατισμός) in spirit, when through Christ himself we have been called (καλέω, perf.) to cessation (κατάληξις) and respite (ἀνακωχή) from every fleshly (σαρκικός) work and wicked (μοχθηρός) pursuits (σπουδάσματα), having shaken off (ἀποσείω) the burden (ἄχθος) of sin, loving withdrawal (ἀπόστασις) from wickedness (φαυλότης) and idleness (ἀργία) from things outside law. For such a Sabbath-keeping was left wanting (ἀπολείπω, impf. pass.) for those from Israel; for they did not at all enter (εἰσβαίνω, perf.) into the rest (κατάπαυσις) of Christ, according to the voice of blessed Paul [Hebrews 4:6–9]. But Christ gave us rest (καταπαύω, aor.) and persuaded (ἀναπείθω) [us] to keep Sabbath intelligibly/spiritually (νοητῶς), being let loose (ἀνίημι, pass.) into virtue and practicing (ἐπιτηδεύω) a good idleness from offenses (πλημμελήματα). PALL.: You spoke excellently. CYR.: But God legislated (θεσμοθετέω) of old that all must be idle (ἀργεῖν) on the Sabbath. Yet those crowned (καταστέφω, perf.) with the divine liturgy (λειτουργία) and ordered to attend (προσεδρεύω) the holy tent (σκηνή) again/still performed (τελέω) the sacred rites; and profaning (βεβηλόω) the Sabbath, according to the Savior's voice [Matthew 12:5], they were blameless (ἀναίτιοι), not undergoing (ὑπομένω) the indictment (γραφή) for having dissolved (λύω) the law. Therefore we ourselves too shall cease (καταλήγω, fut.) from earthly pursuits in Christ, fulfilling (πληρόω) the intelligible (νοητός) Sabbath-keeping, but shall not abstain (ἀπέχομαι, fut.) from the sacred works, I mean the need to bring God spiritual sacrifices and intelligible gift-offerings. Following as it were the footprints (ἴχνη) of Christ, as it is written [1 Peter 2:21], we shall sacrifice (ἱερεύω, fut.) ourselves, honoring the God of all not with sheep-slaughterings (μηλοσφαγίαι) and blood of calves (μόσχοι), but rather dedicating (ἀνατίθημι) ourselves to him for an odour of fragrance (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας). For we shall please (ἀρέσκω, fut.) beyond a young calf producing horns and hoofs (ὁπλαί), according to the Psalmist's voice [Psalm 68:32 LXX]. PALL.: You think rightly (ὀρθῶς διανοῇ); but come (ἴθι) again, and from… [runs into §3].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …Isaiah, who says: ‘The Lord will wash away the filth of the sons and daughters of Zion, and will cleanse the blood from their midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.’ (Isaiah 4:4) So then, Palladius, would we fully carry out the way of the righteousness understood in Christ simply by being scoured clean and by rubbing away our old defilements? Tell me, would that be enough for the glory that befits the saints, and would it crown us with the highest honors? Or rather, will our condition in some way be better, and shall we rightly adorn our own heads with the highest praise, when we bring to God, as a kind of spiritual gift and a truly sacred offering, the life lived in sanctification and holiness, and carry out spiritual worship thoroughly?
Palladius: That is what I say.

Cyril: Indeed this agrees with the sacred laws, is pleasing to God, and is among the things most approved. He commanded rest from all work on the Sabbath, and allowed no one to do anything at all, saying this in Exodus: ‘Remember the day of the Sabbath, to keep it holy. Six days you shall work and do all your works; but the seventh day is the Sabbath, a rest to the Lord your God; you shall do no work on it.’ (Exodus 20:8–10) The type plainly points to the Sabbath rest kept in spirit, when through Christ himself we have been called to cease and rest from every work of the flesh and from wicked pursuits, shaking off the burden of sin, loving to turn away from wickedness and to rest from whatever lies outside the law. For such a Sabbath rest remained out of reach for those of Israel; for they never entered Christ’s rest at all, as blessed Paul says (Hebrews 4:6–9). But Christ has given us rest, and has persuaded us to keep the Sabbath in a spiritual way, giving ourselves freely to virtue and practicing a good idleness from offenses.

Cyril: Now God did indeed lay down long ago that all must rest from work on the Sabbath. Yet those crowned with the divine ministry and appointed to wait on the holy tent still performed the sacred rites; and though they profaned the Sabbath, as the Savior says, they were blameless (Matthew 12:5), and did not face the charge of having broken the law. So we too, in Christ, shall cease from earthly pursuits, fulfilling the inward Sabbath rest; but we shall not hold back from the sacred works — I mean, from our duty to bring God spiritual sacrifices and inward gifts (1 Peter 2:5). Following, as it is written, in the footsteps of Christ (1 Peter 2:21), we shall offer ourselves in sacrifice, honoring the God of all not with slaughtered sheep and the blood of calves, but rather dedicating ourselves to him as a fragrant aroma. For we shall please him more than a young calf that puts forth horns and hoofs, as the Psalmist says (Psalm 69:31).

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 16. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withdrawn English was not used for wording.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.

PG 68.1012. Continues Cyril's sentence from §1. Οὕτω φημί ('So I say') is Palladius agreeing with Cyril's second alternative (that we must also offer a holy life), not with the first. The subject of προστέταχεν and ἠφίει is unexpressed; the masculine λέγων and the preceding Θεῷ κεχαρισμένον point to God, so the English gives 'He'. Ἀπελείπετο … τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσραήλ echoes Hebrews 4:9 (ἀπολείπεται σαββατισμός): rendered 'remained out of reach for those of Israel' to keep Cyril's point that Israel never reached it; Cyril attributes Hebrews to Paul and speaks of 'Christ's rest' where Hebrews says 'His [God's] rest'. Ἡμᾶς δὲ κατέπαυσεν ὁ Χριστός plays on Hebrews 4:8 (εἰ αὐτοὺς Ἰησοῦς κατέπαυσεν), covered by the same citation. Γραφή here is a legal indictment, hence 'face the charge'. Νοητός/νοητῶς (spiritual, perceived by the mind) rendered 'inward' or 'in a spiritual way' to keep it distinct from πνευματικός ('spiritual'). 'Spiritual sacrifices' (θυσίας πνευματικάς) cited to 1 Peter 2:5, the only New Testament source of the phrase; 'following in the footsteps' (ἴχνεσι, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον) to 1 Peter 2:21. Psalm 68:32 LXX = Psalm 69:31 in English Bibles. Εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας is stock sacrificial language (Leviticus passim; compare Ephesians 5:2); left uncited as doubtful. The column cut falls inside Palladius's sentence (καὶ ἐξ / ἱερῶν Γραμμάτων).
